64.     def init_from_json_file(cls, json_filepath):
65.         """Inits the result from the specific model result file"""
66. 
67.         result_file = "/".join(json_filepath.split("/")[2:])
68.         with open(json_filepath) as fp:
69.             data = json.load(fp)
70. 
71.         # We manage the legacy config format
72.         config = _as_dict(data.get("config_general")) or _as_dict(data.get("config"))
73.         task_info = _as_dict(data.get("task_info"))
74.         quantization_config = _as_dict(data.get("quantization_config"))
75.         results_data = _as_dict(data.get("results"))
76. 
77.         model_name = config.get("model_name") or task_info.get("model_name") or data.get("model_name")
78.         if not model_name:
79.             raise ValueError(f"Missing model_name in result file: {json_filepath}")
80. 
81.         # Precision
82.         precision = Precision.from_str(config.get("precision") or task_info.get("precision") or "4bit")
83.         quant_type = QuantType.from_str(str(config.get("quant_type") or task_info.get("quant_type") or "GPTQ"))
84.         weight_dtype = WeightDtype.from_str(task_info.get("weight_dtype") or config.get("weight_dtype") or "int4")
85.         compute_dtype = ComputeDtype.from_str(task_info.get("compute_dtype") or config.get("compute_dtype") or "bfloat16")
86.         
87.         model_params = _safe_round_float(config.get("model_params", data.get("model_params", 0)))
88.         model_size = _safe_round_float(config.get("model_size", data.get("model_size", 0)))
89.         
90.         if quantization_config:
91.             double_quant = quantization_config.get("bnb_4bit_use_double_quant", False)
92.             group_size = quantization_config.get("group_size", -1)
93.         else:
94.             double_quant = False
95.             group_size = -1
96. 
97.         local = config.get("local", False)
98.         if not local:
99.             local = task_info.get("local", False)
100. 
101.         # Get model and org
102.         org_and_model = model_name.split("/", 1)
103. 
104.         if local and org_and_model[0] != "Intel":
105.             org_and_model = model_name.split("/")
106.             org_and_model = ["local", org_and_model[-1]]
107.             quant_type = QuantType.autoround
108. 
109.         if len(org_and_model) == 1:
110.             org = None
111.             model = org_and_model[0]
112.             result_key = f"{model}_{precision.value.name}"
113.         else:
114.             org = org_and_model[0]
115.             model = org_and_model[1]
116.             result_key = f"{org}_{model}_{precision.value.name}"
117.         full_model = "/".join(org_and_model)
118. 
119.         # Extract results
120.         results = {}
121.         for task in Tasks:
122.             task = task.value
123.             if task.benchmark == "mmlu":
124.                 mmlu_data = results_data.get("harness|mmlu|0")
125.                 if mmlu_data is None:
126.                     continue
127.                 accs = np.array([mmlu_data.get(task.metric)])
128.             else:
129.                 accs = np.array(
130.                     [
131.                         v.get(task.metric, None)
132.                         for k, v in results_data.items()
133.                         if task.benchmark in k and isinstance(v, dict)
134.                     ]
135.                 )
136.             if accs.size == 0 or any([acc is None for acc in accs]):
137.                 continue
138. 
139.             mean_acc = np.mean(accs) * 100.0
140.             mean_acc = round(mean_acc, 2)
141.             results[task.benchmark] = mean_acc
142. 
143.         return cls(
144.             eval_name=result_key,
145.             full_model=full_model,
146.             org=org,
147.             model=model,
148.             results=results,
149.             precision=precision,
150.             quant_type=quant_type,
151.             weight_dtype=weight_dtype,
152.             compute_dtype=compute_dtype,
153.             double_quant=double_quant,
154.             revision=config.get("model_sha") or task_info.get("model_sha") or data.get("model_sha", "main"),
155.             num_params=model_params,
156.             model_size=model_size,
157.             group_size=group_size,
158.             result_file=result_file
159.         )

234. def get_request_file_for_model(requests_path, model_name,
235.         quant_type, precision, weight_dtype, compute_dtype):
236.     """Selects the correct request file for a given model. Only keeps runs tagged as FINISHED"""
237.     request_files = os.path.join(
238.         requests_path,
239.         f"{model_name}_eval_request_*.json",
240.     )
241.     request_files = glob.glob(request_files)
242. 
243.     request_file = ""
244.     request_files = sorted(request_files, reverse=True)
245.     for tmp_request_file in request_files:
246.         with open(tmp_request_file, "r") as f:
247.             req_content = json.load(f)
248.             if (
249.                 req_content["status"] in ["Finished"]
250.                 and req_content["precision"] == precision.split(".")[-1]
251.                 and str(req_content["quant_type"]) == quant_type
252.                 and req_content["weight_dtype"] == weight_dtype.split(".")[-1]
253.                 and req_content["compute_dtype"] == compute_dtype.split(".")[-1]
254.             ):
255.                 request_file = tmp_request_file
256.             elif (
257.                 req_content["status"] in ["Finished"]
258.                 and req_content["precision"] == precision.split(".")[-1]
259.                 and quant_type == "AutoRound"
260.                 and req_content["weight_dtype"] == weight_dtype.split(".")[-1]
261.                 and req_content["compute_dtype"] == compute_dtype.split(".")[-1]
262.             ):
263.                 request_file = tmp_request_file
264.     return request_file

267. def get_raw_eval_results(results_path: str, requests_path: str, dynamic_path: str) -> list[EvalResult]:
268.     """From the path of the results folder root, extract all needed info for results"""
269.     model_result_filepaths = []
270. 
271.     for root, _, files in os.walk(results_path):
272.         if len(files) == 0 or any([not f.endswith(".json") for f in files]):
273.             continue
274. 
275.         try:
276.             files.sort(key=lambda x: x.removesuffix(".json").removeprefix("results_")[:-7])
277.         except Exception:
278.             files = [files[-1]]
279. 
280.         for file in files:
281.             model_result_filepaths.append(os.path.join(root, file))
282. 
283.     dynamic_data = {}
284.     if os.path.exists(dynamic_path):
285.         with open(dynamic_path) as f:
286.             dynamic_data = json.load(f)
287. 
288.     eval_results = {}
289.     for model_result_filepath in model_result_filepaths:
290.         try:
291.             eval_result = EvalResult.init_from_json_file(model_result_filepath)
292.             eval_result.update_with_request_file(requests_path)
293.         except Exception as e:
294.             logger.warning("Skipping invalid result file %s: %s", model_result_filepath, e)
295.             logger.debug("Invalid result file traceback", exc_info=True)
296.             continue
297.         
298.         if eval_result.full_model in dynamic_data:
299.             eval_result.update_with_dynamic_file_dict(dynamic_data[eval_result.full_model])
300.             if "meta-llama" in eval_result.full_model: 
301.                 eval_result.still_on_hub = True
302. 
303.         eval_name = eval_result.eval_name
304.         if eval_name in eval_results:
305.             eval_results[eval_name].results.update({k: v for k, v in eval_result.results.items() if v is not None})
306.         else:
307.             eval_results[eval_name] = eval_result
308. 
309.     results = []
310.     for v in eval_results.values():
311.         try:
312.             if v.status == "Finished":
313.                 v.to_dict()  # Validate that to_dict() doesn't raise
314.                 results.append(v)
315.         except Exception as e:
316.             logger.warning("Error processing %s: %s", v.eval_name, e)
317.             continue
318. 
319.     return results

  这是**旧主榜解析器**在扫你新的 aggregate `results_*.json` 时发的 warning，不会导致这次 500；新 tab 会正常读这类结果。
- 后面我复测启动时又遇到一个**新的独立问题**：  
  `src/submission/check_validity.py:23` 这里模块导入时就执行了 `login(token=HF_TOKEN)`，当前环境又碰到了：
  `httpx.ConnectError: [SSL: UNEXPECTED_EOF_WHILE_READING]`  
  这属于 **HF 登录 / 代理 / 网络 SSL** 问题，和这次新 tab 的 `Timestamp` bug 不是一回事。

**结论：**
- 你这份 `err.log` 里的页面 500，主因是 **`Timestamp` 被塞进 Gradio 组件导致 JSON 序列化失败**
- 这个我已经修掉了
- 如果现在还有启动失败，当前剩下的是 **HF 登录的网络/SSL 问题**，不再是 auto pipeline results tab 本身的问题

从展示结果来看，我们的auto_quant运行脚本lb_eval/auto_quant/auto.sh，在upload到github中写的results_*里，没有更新num_gpus，对于quantization+evaluation，需要两个值表示num_gpus,比如quant_num_gpus和eval_num_gpus，对于evaluation only只需要一个num_gpus变量。另外我们做evaluation的tasks，新增三个，piqa, mmlu, hellaswag, gsm8k。
我先把写回链路和展示链路一起改：`auto.sh` 产出正确的 GPU 字段，`upload_results_github.py` 写进 `results_*.json`，leaderboard 新 tab 也同步读出来；同时把默认评测任务扩成 4 个。

88. def _as_dict(value: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
89.     return value if isinstance(value, dict) else {}

92. def _as_list(value: Any) -> list[Any]:
93.     return value if isinstance(value, list) else []
94.

96. def _safe_float(value: Any) -> float | None:
97.     try:
98.         return round(float(value), 2)
99.     except (TypeError, ValueError):
100.         return None

103. def _normalize_task_key(task_name: str) -> str:
104.     normalized = str(task_name).strip().lower().replace("-", "_").replace(" ", "")
105.     return _TASK_ALIASES.get(normalized, normalized)

108. def _score_to_percent(metric_value: Any) -> float | None:
109.     if isinstance(metric_value, dict):
110.         metric_value = metric_value.get("accuracy")
111.     try:
112.         return round(float(metric_value) * 100.0, 2)
113.     except (TypeError, ValueError):
114.         return None

117. def _link_repo(repo_or_url: str | None, label: str) -> str:
118.     if not repo_or_url:
119.         return label
120.     value = str(repo_or_url).strip()
121.     if not value:
122.         return label
123.     if value.startswith("http://") or value.startswith("https://"):
124.         return model_hyperlink(value, label)
125.     return model_hyperlink(f"https://huggingface.co/{value}", label)

128. def _is_auto_pipeline_result(data: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
129.     return isinstance(data, dict) and "generated_at" in data and "run_dir" in data and "copied_files" in data
130. 
131. 
132. def _collect_task_scores(accuracy: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, float | None]:
133.     task_scores: dict[str, float | None] = {task.value.col_name: None for task in Tasks}
134.     raw_tasks = _as_dict(accuracy.get("tasks"))
135.     normalized_scores = {_normalize_task_key(name): _score_to_percent(value) for name, value in raw_tasks.items()}
136. 
137.     for task in Tasks:
138.         task_scores[task.value.col_name] = normalized_scores.get(task.value.benchmark)
139. 
140.     return task_scores

143. def get_auto_pipeline_results_df(results_path: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
144.     rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
145. 
146.     for root, _, files in os.walk(results_path):
147.         for filename in files:
148.             if not (filename.startswith("results_") and filename.endswith(".json")):
149.                 continue
150. 
151.             result_path = os.path.join(root, filename)
152.             try:
153.                 with open(result_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
154.                     data = json.load(handle)
155.             except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
156.                 logger.warning("Skipping malformed auto pipeline result %s: %s", result_path, exc)
157.                 continue
158. 
159.             if not _is_auto_pipeline_result(data):
160.                 continue
161. 
162.             quant_summary = _as_dict(data.get("quant_summary"))
163.             accuracy = _as_dict(data.get("accuracy"))
164.             pipeline = "auto_quant" if quant_summary else "auto_eval"
165.             model_id = str(data.get("model_id") or "")
166.             artifact_name = str(data.get("artifact_name") or model_id or os.path.splitext(filename)[0])
167.             hf_repo = quant_summary.get("hf_repo")
168.             artifact_repo = hf_repo or model_id
169.             copied_files = [str(path) for path in _as_list(data.get("copied_files"))]
170.             output_files = [str(path) for path in _as_list(quant_summary.get("output_files"))]
171.             all_artifact_paths = [path.lower() for path in copied_files + output_files]
172. 
173.             has_logs = any(path.endswith("/logs") or "/logs/" in path or path.endswith("/logs/auto.log") for path in all_artifact_paths)
174.             has_sessions = any("/session_" in path or os.path.basename(path).startswith("session_") for path in all_artifact_paths)
175.             has_quantize_script = any(
176.                 path.endswith("quantize.py") or path.endswith("quantize_script.py") for path in all_artifact_paths
177.             )
178. 
179.             task_scores = _collect_task_scores(accuracy)
180.             valid_scores = [score for score in task_scores.values() if score is not None]
181.             average_score = round(sum(valid_scores) / len(valid_scores), 2) if valid_scores else None
182. 
183.             relative_result_path = os.path.relpath(result_path, results_path)
184.             generated_at = data.get("generated_at")
185.             search_text = " ".join(
186.                 filter(
187.                     None,
188.                     [
189.                         pipeline,
190.                         model_id,
191.                         artifact_name,
192.                         str(hf_repo or ""),
193.                         str(data.get("run_dir") or ""),
194.                         str(quant_summary.get("scheme") or accuracy.get("scheme") or ""),
195.                         str(quant_summary.get("method") or ""),
196.                         str(accuracy.get("eval_framework") or ""),
197.                     ],
198.                 )
199.             )
200. 
201.             row = {
202.                 "Pipeline": pipeline,
203.                 "Model": _link_repo(model_id, model_id or artifact_name),
204.                 "Artifact": _link_repo(artifact_repo, artifact_name),
205.                 "Generated At": generated_at,
206.                 "Average ⬆️": average_score,
207.                 "Quant Status": quant_summary.get("status") or "missing",
208.                 "Eval Status": accuracy.get("status") or "missing",
209.                 "Scheme": quant_summary.get("scheme") or accuracy.get("scheme"),
210.                 "Method": quant_summary.get("method"),
211.                 "Export Format": quant_summary.get("export_format"),
212.                 "Eval Framework": accuracy.get("eval_framework"),
213.                 "Quant Secs": _safe_float(quant_summary.get("duration_seconds")),
214.                 "Eval Secs": _safe_float(accuracy.get("duration_seconds")),
215.                 "Original MB": _safe_float(quant_summary.get("original_size_mb")),
216.                 "Quantized MB": _safe_float(quant_summary.get("quantized_size_mb")),
217.                 "Compression": _safe_float(quant_summary.get("compression_ratio")),
218.                 "GPUs": quant_summary.get("num_gpus") or accuracy.get("num_gpus"),
219.                 "Logs": has_logs,
220.                 "Sessions": has_sessions,
221.                 "quantize.py": has_quantize_script,
222.                 "Artifacts": len(copied_files),
223.                 "Run Dir": data.get("run_dir"),
224.                 "Result JSON": relative_result_path,
225.                 AUTO_PIPELINE_SEARCH_COL: search_text,
226.                 AUTO_PIPELINE_SORT_COL: generated_at,
227.             }
228.             row.update(task_scores)
229.             rows.append(row)
230. 
231.     if not rows:
232.         return pd.DataFrame(columns=AUTO_PIPELINE_ALL_COLUMNS + [AUTO_PIPELINE_SEARCH_COL, AUTO_PIPELINE_SORT_COL])
233. 
234.     df = pd.DataFrame.from_records(rows)
235.     for col in AUTO_PIPELINE_ALL_COLUMNS + [AUTO_PIPELINE_SEARCH_COL, AUTO_PIPELINE_SORT_COL]:
236.         if col not in df.columns:
237.             df[col] = None
238. 
239.     df[AUTO_PIPELINE_SORT_COL] = df[AUTO_PIPELINE_SORT_COL].fillna("").astype(str)
240.     df = df.sort_values(by=AUTO_PIPELINE_SORT_COL, ascending=False, na_position="last").reset_index(drop=True)
241.     return df[AUTO_PIPELINE_ALL_COLUMNS + [AUTO_PIPELINE_SEARCH_COL, AUTO_PIPELINE_SORT_COL]]
242.

1. #!/usr/bin/env python3
2. """
3. Upload auto_quant result artifacts into the lb_eval GitHub repository.
4. 
5. Artifacts copied from the runtime output directory:
6. - quant_summary.json / summary.json
7. - accuracy.json
8. - quantize.py
9. - logs/
10. - session_*.jsonl
11. - session_*.md
12. 
13. Layout:
14. results/<org>/<artifact_name>/results_<timestamp>.json
15. results/<org>/<artifact_name>/run_<timestamp>/...
16. """

31. def utc_now() -> str:

43. def looks_like_quantized_artifact(model_short: str) -> bool:
44.     lowered = model_short.lower()
45.     markers = (
46.         "-autoround-",
47.         "-gptq",
48.         "-awq",
49.         ".gguf",
50.         "-gguf",
51.         "llm-compressor",
52.     )

56. def run_git(args: list[str], cwd: Path, check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
57.     return subprocess.run(
58.         ["git", *args],
59.         cwd=str(cwd),
60.         text=True,
61.         capture_output=True,
62.         check=check,
63.     )

66. def clone_repo(repo_url: str, target_dir: Path) -> None:
67.     target_dir.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
68.     result = subprocess.run(
69.         ["git", "clone", repo_url, str(target_dir)],
70.         text=True,
71.         capture_output=True,
72.         check=False,
73.     )
74.     if result.returncode != 0:
75.         raise RuntimeError(result.stderr.strip() or result.stdout.strip() or "git clone failed")

78. def ensure_git_config(repo_dir: Path, user_name: str, user_email: str) -> None:
79.     run_git(["config", "user.name", user_name], repo_dir)
80.     run_git(["config", "user.email", user_email], repo_dir)

83. def build_auth_url(repo_url: str, token: str | None) -> str:
84.     if not token:
85.         return repo_url
86.     parts = urlsplit(repo_url)
87.     if parts.scheme != "https":
88.         return repo_url
89.     netloc = f"x-access-token:***REDACTED***@{parts.netloc}"
90.     return urlunsplit((parts.scheme, netloc, parts.path, parts.query, parts.fragment))

93. def load_json(path: Path) -> dict | None:
94.     if not path.exists():
95.         return None

100. def copy_file(src: Path, dst: Path, copied: list[str]) -> None:
101.     if not src.exists() or not src.is_file():
102.         return
103.     dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
104.     shutil.copy2(src, dst)
105.     copied.append(str(dst))

108. def copy_tree(src: Path, dst: Path, copied: list[str]) -> None:
109.     if not src.exists() or not src.is_dir():
110.         return
111.     if dst.exists():
112.         shutil.rmtree(dst)
113.     shutil.copytree(src, dst)
114.     copied.append(str(dst))

117. def detect_artifact_name(model_id: str, scheme: str, quant_summary: dict | None) -> str:
118.     if quant_summary:
119.         hf_repo = quant_summary.get("hf_repo")
120.         if isinstance(hf_repo, str) and hf_repo.strip():
121.             return hf_repo.rstrip("/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
122. 
123.     model_short = model_id.split("/", 1)[-1] if "/" in model_id else model_id
124.     if looks_like_quantized_artifact(model_short):
125.         return sanitize_name(model_short)
126.     return sanitize_name(f"{model_short}-autoround-{scheme}")

129. def resolve_repo_dir(repo_dir_arg: str, clone_dir_arg: str, repo_url: str, token: str | None) -> Path:
130.     repo_dir_raw = (repo_dir_arg or "").strip()
131.     clone_dir_raw = (clone_dir_arg or "").strip()
132.     default_clone_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "lb_eval"
133. 
134.     if repo_dir_raw:
135.         repo_dir = Path(repo_dir_raw).resolve()
136.     else:
137.         repo_dir = Path(clone_dir_raw).resolve() if clone_dir_raw else default_clone_dir.resolve()
138. 
139.     if (repo_dir / ".git").exists():
140.         return repo_dir
141. 
142.     if repo_dir.exists():
143.         if any(repo_dir.iterdir()):
144.             raise RuntimeError(f"target repo dir exists but is not a git repo: {repo_dir}")
145.     else:
146.         repo_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
147. 
148.     if not repo_url:
149.         raise RuntimeError("GIT_REPO is required when the local git repo is missing")
150. 
151.     auth_url = build_auth_url(repo_url, token)
152.     print(f"[github-upload] Cloning repo into: {repo_dir}")
153.     shutil.rmtree(repo_dir)
154.     clone_repo(auth_url, repo_dir)
155.     if auth_url != repo_url:
156.         run_git(["remote", "set-url", "origin", repo_url], repo_dir)
157.     return repo_dir

160. def main() -> int:
161.     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Upload result artifacts to the lb_eval GitHub repo")
162.     parser.add_argument("runtime_output_dir", help="Directory containing quant/eval runtime artifacts")
163.     parser.add_argument("model_id", help="Original model id, e.g. Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B")
164.     parser.add_argument("--scheme", default="W4A16", help="Quantization scheme label")
165.     parser.add_argument(
166.         "--model-output-dir",
167.         default="",
168.         help="Optional model directory associated with this runtime output",
169.     )
170.     parser.add_argument(
171.         "--repo-dir",
172.         default=os.environ.get(
173.             "GIT_RESULTS_REPO_DIR",
174.             "",
175.         ),
176.         help="Local clone of the lb_eval git repo. If empty or missing, the repo is cloned automatically.",
177.     )
178.     parser.add_argument(
179.         "--clone-dir",
180.         default=os.environ.get("GIT_RESULTS_CLONE_DIR") or str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "lb_eval"),
181.         help="Clone destination used when --repo-dir is empty or missing",
182.     )
183.     parser.add_argument(
184.         "--git-repo",
185.         default=os.environ.get("GIT_REPO", ""),
186.         help="Remote git repo URL used for authenticated pull/push when token is provided",
187.     )
188.     parser.add_argument(
189.         "--git-token",
190.         default=os.environ.get("GIT_TOKEN", ""),
191.         help="GitHub token used for authenticated push",
192.     )
193.     parser.add_argument(
194.         "--branch",
195.         default=os.environ.get("GIT_BRANCH", ""),
196.         help="Branch to update. Defaults to current branch.",
197.     )
198.     parser.add_argument(
199.         "--dry-run",
200.         action="store_true",
201.         help="Prepare artifact files locally but do not create a commit or push",
202.     )
203.     parser.add_argument(
204.         "--git-user-name",
205.         default=os.environ.get("GIT_USER_NAME", "lb-eval-bot"),
206.         help="git config user.name for generated commits",
207.     )
208.     parser.add_argument(
209.         "--git-user-email",
210.         default=os.environ.get("GIT_USER_EMAIL", "lb-eval-bot@local"),
211.         help="git config user.email for generated commits",
212.     )
213.     args = parser.parse_args()
214. 
215.     runtime_output_dir = Path(args.runtime_output_dir).resolve()
216.     if not runtime_output_dir.is_dir():
217.         print(f"ERROR: runtime output directory not found: {runtime_output_dir}")
218.         return 1
219. 
220.     model_output_dir = None
221.     if args.model_output_dir.strip():
222.         model_output_dir = Path(args.model_output_dir).resolve()
223. 
224.     try:
225.         repo_dir = resolve_repo_dir(args.repo_dir, args.clone_dir, args.git_repo, args.git_token or None)
226.     except Exception as exc:
227.         print(f"ERROR: could not prepare git repo: {exc}")
228.         return 1
229. 
230.     quant_summary_path = runtime_output_dir / "quant_summary.json"
231.     summary_path = runtime_output_dir / "summary.json"
232.     accuracy_path = runtime_output_dir / "accuracy.json"
233.     quantize_script_path = runtime_output_dir / "quantize.py"
234.     legacy_quantize_script_path = runtime_output_dir / "quantize_script.py"

238.

241.     timestamp = file_timestamp()

246. 
247.     print(f"[github-upload] repo dir: {repo_dir}")
248.     print(f"[github-upload] model id: {args.model_id}")
249.     print(f"[github-upload] artifact name: {artifact_name}")
250.     print(f"[github-upload] result org: {org}")
251.     print(f"[github-upload] branch: {branch}")
252.     ensure_git_config(repo_dir, args.git_user_name, args.git_user_email)
253.     print(f"[github-upload] git user: {args.git_user_name} <{args.git_user_email}>")
254.     if not args.dry_run:
255.         remote_url = args.git_repo or run_git(["remote", "get-url", "origin"], repo_dir).stdout.strip()
256.         auth_url = build_auth_url(remote_url, args.git_token or None)
257.         pull_target = auth_url if args.git_token else "origin"
258.         push_target = auth_url if args.git_token else "origin"
259. 
260.         pull_args = ["pull", "--rebase", pull_target, branch]
261.         pull_result = run_git(pull_args, repo_dir, check=False)
262.         if pull_result.returncode != 0:
263.             print(f"[github-upload] ERROR: git pull failed:\n{pull_result.stderr.strip()}")
264.             return 1
265. 
266.     model_result_dir = repo_dir / "results" / org / artifact_name
267.     run_dir = model_result_dir / f"run_{timestamp}"
268.     run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
269. 
270.     copied: list[str] = []
271.     copy_file(quant_summary_path, run_dir / "quant_summary.json", copied)
272.     copy_file(summary_path, run_dir / "summary.json", copied)
273.     copy_file(accuracy_path, run_dir / "accuracy.json", copied)
274.     if quantize_script_path.is_file():
275.         copy_file(quantize_script_path, run_dir / "quantize.py", copied)
276.     elif legacy_quantize_script_path.is_file():
277.         copy_file(legacy_quantize_script_path, run_dir / "quantize.py", copied)
278.     copy_tree(logs_dir, run_dir / "logs", copied)
279. 
280.     for path in sorted(runtime_output_dir.glob("session_*.jsonl")):
281.         copy_file(path, run_dir / path.name, copied)
282.     for path in sorted(runtime_output_dir.glob("session_*.md")):
283.         copy_file(path, run_dir / path.name, copied)
284. 
285.     aggregate = {
286.         "model_id": args.model_id,
287.         "artifact_name": artifact_name,
288.         "generated_at": utc_now(),
289.         "source_runtime_dir": str(runtime_output_dir),
290.         "source_model_dir": str(model_output_dir) if model_output_dir else None,
291.         "run_dir": str(run_dir.relative_to(repo_dir)),
292.         "quant_summary": quant_summary,
293.         "accuracy": accuracy,
294.         "copied_files": [str(Path(path).relative_to(repo_dir)) for path in copied],
295.     }
296.     aggregate_path = model_result_dir / f"results_{timestamp}.json"
297.     aggregate_path.write_text(json.dumps(aggregate, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
298.     copied.append(str(aggregate_path))
299. 
300.     rel_paths = [str(Path(path).relative_to(repo_dir)) for path in copied]
301.     if not rel_paths:
302.         print("[github-upload] No artifacts found to upload.")
303.         return 0
304. 
305.     if args.dry_run:
306.         print("[github-upload] Dry run prepared artifacts:")
307.         for rel_path in rel_paths:
308.             print(f"  - {rel_path}")
309.         return 0
310. 
311.     run_git(["add", *rel_paths], repo_dir)
312.     diff_result = run_git(["diff", "--cached", "--quiet"], repo_dir, check=False)
313.     if diff_result.returncode == 0:
314.         print("[github-upload] No changes to commit.")
315.         return 0
316. 
317.     commit_message = (
318.         f"Add auto_quant artifacts for {artifact_name}\n\n"
319.         "Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>"
320.     )
321.     commit_result = run_git(["commit", "-m", commit_message], repo_dir, check=False)
322.     if commit_result.returncode != 0:
323.         print(f"[github-upload] ERROR: git commit failed:\n{commit_result.stderr.strip()}")
324.         return 1
325. 
326.     push_args = ["push", push_target, f"HEAD:{branch}"]
327.     push_result = run_git(push_args, repo_dir, check=False)
328.     if push_result.returncode != 0:
329.         print(f"[github-upload] ERROR: git push failed:\n{push_result.stderr.strip()}")
330.         return 1
331. 
332.     print("[github-upload] Uploaded artifacts:")
333.     for rel_path in rel_paths:
334.         print(f"  - {rel_path}")
335.     return 0
336. 
337. 
338. if __name__ == "__main__":
339.     raise SystemExit(main())

1. # auto_quant Developer Guide
2. 
3. This document describes the `tasks/lb_eval/auto_quant` workflow: required environment variables, script responsibilities, runtime flow, and artifact layout.
4. 
5. ## 1. Scope
6. 
7. The `auto_quant` workflow is the container-side entrypoint used to:
8. 
9. 1. Read a quantization/evaluation request JSON
10. 2. Run quantization with OpenClaw
11. 3. Run evaluation with OpenClaw
12. 4. Upload the quantized model to Hugging Face
13. 5. Write result artifacts back to the `lb_eval` GitHub repository
14. 
15. The current implementation separates:
16. 
17. - **Model output dir**: only quantized model files
18. - **Runtime output dir**: logs, prompts, request copies, sessions, summaries, evaluation output, venv
19. 
20. This avoids runtime artifacts being removed when quantization/export rewrites the model directory.
21. 
22. ## 2. Main scripts
23. 
24. | Script | Purpose |
25. | --- | --- |
26. | `run_pod.sh` | Build the image and start the container |
27. | `auto.sh` | Main entrypoint inside the container |
28. | `format_sessions.py` | Convert OpenClaw session JSONL files to Markdown |
29. | `upload_model_hf.py` | Upload quantized model directory to Hugging Face |
30. | `hf_shared_ledger.py` | Shared git-backed ledger for multi-machine HF account coordination |
31. | `upload_results_github.py` | Copy runtime artifacts into the `lb_eval` GitHub results repo and push |
32. 
33. ## 3. Typical run sequence
34. 
35. ### 3.1 Start the container
36. 
37. Run on the host:
38. 
39. ```bash
40. cd /root/leaderboard_Agent/tasks/lb_eval
41. bash run_pod.sh
42. ```
43. 
44. If needed, configure the container name, image name, or output mount via the environment before running `run_pod.sh`.
45. 
46. ### 3.2 Run auto_quant inside the container
47. 
48. ```bash
49. cd /root/leaderboard_Agent/tasks/lb_eval/auto_quant
50. bash auto.sh Qwen3-0.6B_quant_request_False_W4A16_4bit_int4.json
51. ```
52. 
53. Optional flags:
54. 
55. ```bash
56. bash auto.sh <task.json> --dry-run
57. bash auto.sh <task.json> --skip-upload
58. bash auto.sh <task.json> --skip-hf
59. bash auto.sh <task.json> --skip-github
60. ```
61. 
62. ## 4. Runtime flow
63. 
64. `auto.sh` performs the following steps:
65. 
66. 1. Load `config.env`
67. 2. Parse the request JSON and derive:
68.    - pipeline type
69.    - model id
70.    - quantization scheme
71.    - quant/eval GPU counts
72. 3. Resolve OpenClaw workspace and session directories
73. 4. Resolve:
74.    - **model output dir**
75.    - **runtime output dir**
76. 5. Start unified logging to `logs/auto.log`
77. 6. Copy the input request JSON into the runtime output dir
78. 7. If quantization has not already succeeded:
79.    - generate quant prompt
80.    - run `openclaw agent --local`
81.    - expect `quant_summary.json`
82. 8. Copy quant session JSONL from the OpenClaw sessions directory
83. 9. If evaluation has not already succeeded and quantization succeeded:
84.    - generate eval prompt
85.    - use `auto_eval` for the quantization+evaluation flow, or `auto_eval_vllm` for evaluation-only requests
86.    - run `openclaw agent --local`
87.    - expect `accuracy.json`
88. 10. Copy eval session JSONL
89. 11. Format copied session JSONL files into Markdown
90. 12. If enabled and quantization succeeded:
91.    - upload model directory to Hugging Face
92. 13. If enabled:
93.    - upload runtime artifacts to the GitHub results repo
94. 14. Exit non-zero if any required stage failed
95. 
96. ### Important behavior
97. 
98. - All shell output is written to one log: `logs/auto.log`
99. - Step failures are recorded and the script continues when possible
100. - The final exit code still reflects pipeline failure
101. - Prompt files are saved as runtime artifacts, but prompt text is generated in memory first
102. 
103. ## 5. Directory layout
104. 
105. Assume:
106. 
107. - `OUTPUT_DIR=/root/.openclaw/workspace/quantized`
108. - model slug = `Qwen_Qwen3-0.6B`
109. - scheme = `W4A16`
110. 
111. Then:
112. 
113. ```text
114. Model output dir:
115. /root/.openclaw/workspace/quantized/Qwen_Qwen3-0.6B-W4A16
116. 
117. Runtime output dir:
118. /root/.openclaw/workspace/quantized/runs/Qwen_Qwen3-0.6B-W4A16
119. ```
120. 
121. ### Model output dir
122. 
123. Expected contents:
124. 
125. - quantized weights
126. - tokenizer/config files
127. - model metadata required for inference/upload
128. 
129. This directory is the source for Hugging Face model upload.

131. ### Runtime output dir
132. 
133. Expected contents:
134. 
135. - `logs/auto.log`
136. - `logs/quant_prompt.txt`
137. - `logs/eval_prompt.txt`
138. - `request.json`
139. - `quant_summary.json`
140. - `accuracy.json`
141. - `session_quant_<pid>.jsonl`
142. - `session_eval_<pid>.jsonl`
143. - `session_quant_<pid>.md`
144. - `session_eval_<pid>.md`
145. - `venv/` created and reused by the OpenClaw tasks when needed
146. 
147. This directory is the source for GitHub artifact upload.

149. ## 6. Environment variables
150. 
151. The workflow reads `tasks/lb_eval/auto_quant/config.env`.
152. 
153. Do **not** put real secrets in documentation or commit them to git. Use local-only values or secret injection in your runtime.
154. 
155. ### 6.1 Hugging Face upload
156. 
157. | Variable | Required | Purpose |
158. | --- | --- | --- |
159. | `HF_TOKENS` | Yes, if HF upload is enabled | Comma-separated Hugging Face tokens |
160. | `HF_UPLOAD_ORGS` | Recommended | Comma-separated org/user names matching the tokens |
161. | `HF_ACCOUNT_IDS` | Optional | Stable logical account ids for ledger accounting |
162. | `HF_ACCOUNT_CAPACITY_GB` | Optional | Per-account capacity assumption used by the ledger |
163. | `HF_USAGE_FILE` | Optional | Local JSON ledger path for non-shared mode |
164. 
165. ### 6.2 Shared Hugging Face ledger
166. 
167. Used when multiple workers or machines share the same HF accounts.
168. 
169. | Variable | Required | Purpose |
170. | --- | --- | --- |
171. | `HF_SHARED_LEDGER_ENABLED` | Optional | Enable shared ledger mode |
172. | `HF_SHARED_LEDGER_REPO` | Yes in shared mode | Git-backed ledger repo, usually a HF dataset repo or other git remote |
173. | `HF_SHARED_LEDGER_TOKEN` | Usually yes | Token used to clone/pull/push the ledger repo |
174. | `HF_SHARED_LEDGER_BRANCH` | Optional | Branch used by the ledger repo |
175. | `HF_SHARED_LEDGER_CLONE_DIR` | Optional | Local cache/clone path for the shared ledger repo |
176. | `HF_SHARED_LEDGER_RESERVATION_TTL_SECONDS` | Optional | Reservation expiry time |
177. | `HF_SHARED_LEDGER_GIT_USER_NAME` | Optional | Git author name for ledger commits |
178. | `HF_SHARED_LEDGER_GIT_USER_EMAIL` | Optional | Git author email for ledger commits |
179. 
180. ### 6.3 GitHub results upload
181. 
182. | Variable | Required | Purpose |
183. | --- | --- | --- |
184. | `GIT_TOKEN` | Yes, if GitHub upload is enabled | Token used for authenticated push |
185. | `GIT_REPO` | Yes when repo must be cloned | Remote `lb_eval` repo URL |
186. | `GIT_BRANCH` | Optional | Target branch |
187. | `GIT_RESULTS_REPO_DIR` | Optional | Existing local clone of the results repo |
188. | `GIT_RESULTS_CLONE_DIR` | Optional | Clone destination when no local repo is provided |
189. | `GIT_USER_NAME` | Optional | Git author name for result commits |
190. | `GIT_USER_EMAIL` | Optional | Git author email for result commits |
191. 
192. ### 6.4 OpenClaw / runtime
193. 
194. | Variable | Required | Purpose |
195. | --- | --- | --- |
196. | `MINIMAX_API_KEY` | Usually yes | API key used by OpenClaw agent |
197. | `HTTP_PROXY` | Optional | HTTP proxy |
198. | `HTTPS_PROXY` | Optional | HTTPS proxy |
199. | `OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR` | Recommended | OpenClaw portable workspace root; used to resolve skills |
200. | `OPENCLAW_SESSIONS_DIR` | Recommended | Directory containing OpenClaw session JSONL files |
201. 
202. If `OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR` is empty, `auto.sh` auto-detects it in this order:
203. 
204. 1. `/root/leaderboard_Agent/auto_quant/openclaw_home/workspace`
205. 2. `/root/leaderboard_Agent/tasks/lb_eval/openclaw_config/workspace`
206. 3. `/root/.openclaw/workspace`
207. 
208. ### 6.5 Pipeline defaults
209. 
210. | Variable | Required | Purpose |
211. | --- | --- | --- |
212. | `METHOD` | Optional | Quantization method label passed into the prompt |
213. | `EXPORT_FORMAT` | Optional | Export format label passed into the prompt |
214. | `DEVICE` | Optional | Runtime device, usually `cuda` |
215. | `DEVICE_INDEX` | Optional | Device index used in the eval summary |
216. | `TIMEOUT` | Optional | OpenClaw agent timeout |
217. | `EVAL_TASKS` | Optional | Evaluation tasks, e.g. `piqa` |
218. | `EVAL_BATCH_SIZE` | Optional | Evaluation batch size |
219. 
220. ### 6.6 Output directories
221. 
222. | Variable | Required | Purpose |
223. | --- | --- | --- |
224. | `OUTPUT_DIR` | Optional | Base directory for quantized model export |
225. | `RUNTIME_OUTPUT_BASE_DIR` | Optional | Base directory for runtime artifacts |
226. 
227. Defaults:
228. 
229. - `OUTPUT_DIR=/root/.openclaw/workspace/quantized`
230. - `RUNTIME_OUTPUT_BASE_DIR=/root/.openclaw/workspace/quantized/runs`
231. 
232. ### 6.7 Container startup
233. 
234. Used mainly by `run_pod.sh`.
235. 
236. | Variable | Required | Purpose |
237. | --- | --- | --- |
238. | `IMAGE_NAME` | Optional | Docker image name |
239. | `CONTAINER_NAME` | Optional | Docker container name |
240. | `CONTAINER_OUTPUT_DIR` | Optional | Container-side path used for output volume mount |
241. | `DOCKER_EXTRA_ARGS` | Optional | Extra arguments passed to `docker run` |
242. 
243. ## 7. Request JSON expectations
244. 
245. `auto.sh` expects a JSON file containing fields such as:
246. 
247. | Field | Purpose |
248. | --- | --- |
249. | `script` | Determines whether the pipeline is `auto_quant` or `auto_eval` |
250. | `job_type` | Used as an additional signal for pipeline selection |
251. | `model` | Model id, e.g. `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` |
252. | `revision` | Model revision |
253. | `quant_scheme` or `compute_dtype` | Used to derive `W4A16`-style scheme label |
254. | `quant_gpu_nums` | Quantization GPU count |
255. | `eval_gpu_nums` | Evaluation GPU count |
256. | `quant_precision` | Precision label |
257. | `quant_weight_dtype` | Weight dtype label |
258.

38. def _normalize_queue_entry(data: dict) -> dict:
39.     """Normalize queue JSON keys to match EvalQueueColumn/QuantQueueColumn field names.
40. 
41.     Handles mismatches between:
42.       - JSON 'weight_dtype' → column 'weight_type'
43.       - Quant entries with 'quant_precision' but no 'precision'
44.     """
45.     if "weight_type" not in data and "weight_dtype" in data:
46.         data["weight_type"] = data["weight_dtype"]
47.     if "precision" not in data and "quant_precision" in data:
48.         data["precision"] = data["quant_precision"]
49.     return data

52. def _load_queue_entries(save_path: str, request_type: str = None) -> list[dict]:
53.     """Load all queue JSON entries from *save_path* (including subdirectories).
54. 
55.     Args:
56.         save_path: Directory containing queue JSON files.
57.         request_type: Optional filter — ``"eval"`` keeps only ``_eval_request_``
58.             files, ``"quant"`` keeps only ``_quant_request_`` files.
59.             ``None`` keeps all files (backward-compatible).
60. 
61.     Returns:
62.         List of loaded & normalized dicts.
63.     """
64.     entries = [e for e in os.listdir(save_path) if not e.startswith(".")]
65.     all_evals = []
66. 
67.     def _process_file(file_path: str):
68.         fname = os.path.basename(file_path)
69.         if request_type == "eval" and "_quant_request_" in fname:
70.             return
71.         if request_type == "quant" and "_eval_request_" in fname:
72.             return
73. 
74.         try:
75.             with open(file_path) as fp:
76.                 data = json.load(fp)
77.         except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as e:
78.             logger.warning("Skipping malformed queue file %s: %s", file_path, e)
79.             return
80. 
81.         data[eval_queue_cols.model.name] = make_clickable_model(data["model"])
82.         data[eval_queue_cols.revision.name] = data.get("revision", "main")
83.         _normalize_queue_entry(data)
84.         all_evals.append(data)
85. 
86.     for entry in entries:
87.         full_path = os.path.join(save_path, entry)
88.         if entry.endswith(".json"):
89.             _process_file(full_path)
90.         elif os.path.isdir(full_path):
91.             sub_entries = [e for e in os.listdir(full_path) if not e.startswith(".")]
92.             for sub_entry in sub_entries:
93.                 if sub_entry.endswith(".json"):
94.                     _process_file(os.path.join(full_path, sub_entry))
95. 
96.     return all_evals
97.

99. def _split_by_status(all_evals: list[dict]) -> tuple[list, list, list]:
100.     """Split entries into (pending, running, finished) lists by status."""
101.     pending  = [e for e in all_evals if e.get("status") in ("Pending", "Rerun", "Waiting")]
102.     running  = [e for e in all_evals if e.get("status") == "Running"]
103.     finished = [e for e in all_evals
104.                 if e.get("status", "").startswith("Finished")
105.                 or e.get("status") == "PENDING_NEW_EVAL"]
106.     return pending, running, finished
107. 
108. 
109. def _build_queue_dfs(pending: list, running: list, finished: list,
110.                      cols: list) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
111.     """Build DataFrames from split lists, keeping only the requested *cols*."""
112.     all_records = pending + running + finished
113.     if all_records:
114.         existing_cols = [c for c in cols if c in pd.DataFrame(all_records).columns]
115.     else:
116.         existing_cols = cols
117. 
118.     df_finished = pd.DataFrame.from_records(finished, columns=existing_cols)
119.     df_running  = pd.DataFrame.from_records(running,  columns=existing_cols)
120.     df_pending  = pd.DataFrame.from_records(pending,  columns=existing_cols)
121. 
122.     return df_finished[existing_cols], df_running[existing_cols], df_pending[existing_cols]
123. 
124. 
125. def get_evaluation_queue_df(save_path: str, cols: list,
126.                             request_type: str = None) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
127.     """Load evaluation queue and split into (finished, running, pending) DataFrames.
128. 
129.     Args:
130.         save_path: Directory containing queue JSON files.
131.         cols: Column names to keep in the output DataFrames.
132.         request_type: ``"eval"``, ``"quant"``, or ``None`` (all).
133.     """
134.     all_evals = _load_queue_entries(save_path, request_type=request_type)
135.     pending, running, finished = _split_by_status(all_evals)
136.     return _build_queue_dfs(pending, running, finished, cols)

234. def get_request_file_for_model(requests_path, model_name,
235.         quant_type, precision, weight_dtype, compute_dtype):
236.     """Selects the correct request file for a given model. Only keeps runs tagged as FINISHED"""
237.     request_files = os.path.join(
238.         requests_path,
239.         f"{model_name}_eval_request_*.json",
240.     )
241.     request_files = glob.glob(request_files)
242. 
243.     request_file = ""
244.     request_files = sorted(request_files, reverse=True)
245.     for tmp_request_file in request_files:
246.         with open(tmp_request_file, "r") as f:
247.             req_content = json.load(f)
248.             if (
249.                 req_content["status"] in ["Finished"]
250.                 and req_content["precision"] == precision.split(".")[-1]
251.                 and str(req_content["quant_type"]) == quant_type
252.                 and req_content["weight_dtype"] == weight_dtype.split(".")[-1]
253.                 and req_content["compute_dtype"] == compute_dtype.split(".")[-1]
254.             ):
255.                 request_file = tmp_request_file
256.             elif (
257.                 req_content["status"] in ["Finished"]
258.                 and req_content["precision"] == precision.split(".")[-1]
259.                 and quant_type == "AutoRound"
260.                 and req_content["weight_dtype"] == weight_dtype.split(".")[-1]
261.                 and req_content["compute_dtype"] == compute_dtype.split(".")[-1]
262.             ):
263.                 request_file = tmp_request_file
264.     return request_file

267. def get_raw_eval_results(results_path: str, requests_path: str, dynamic_path: str) -> list[EvalResult]:
268.     """From the path of the results folder root, extract all needed info for results"""
269.     model_result_filepaths = []
270. 
271.     for root, _, files in os.walk(results_path):
272.         if len(files) == 0 or any([not f.endswith(".json") for f in files]):
273.             continue
274. 
275.         try:
276.             files.sort(key=lambda x: x.removesuffix(".json").removeprefix("results_")[:-7])
277.         except Exception:
278.             files = [files[-1]]
279. 
280.         for file in files:
281.             model_result_filepaths.append(os.path.join(root, file))
282. 
283.     dynamic_data = {}
284.     if os.path.exists(dynamic_path):
285.         with open(dynamic_path) as f:
286.             dynamic_data = json.load(f)
287. 
288.     eval_results = {}
289.     for model_result_filepath in model_result_filepaths:
290.         try:
291.             eval_result = EvalResult.init_from_json_file(model_result_filepath)
292.             eval_result.update_with_request_file(requests_path)
293.         except Exception as e:
294.             logger.warning("Skipping invalid result file %s: %s", model_result_filepath, e)
295.             logger.debug("Invalid result file traceback", exc_info=True)
296.             continue
297.         
298.         if eval_result.full_model in dynamic_data:
299.             eval_result.update_with_dynamic_file_dict(dynamic_data[eval_result.full_model])
300.             if "meta-llama" in eval_result.full_model: 
301.                 eval_result.still_on_hub = True
302. 
303.         eval_name = eval_result.eval_name
304.         if eval_name in eval_results:
305.             eval_results[eval_name].results.update({k: v for k, v in eval_result.results.items() if v is not None})
306.         else:
307.             eval_results[eval_name] = eval_result
308. 
309.     results = []
310.     for v in eval_results.values():
311.         try:
312.             if v.status == "Finished":
313.                 v.to_dict()  # Validate that to_dict() doesn't raise
314.                 results.append(v)
315.         except Exception as e:
316.             logger.warning("Error processing %s: %s", v.eval_name, e)
317.             continue
318. 
319.     return results

原因找到了：**被 skip 的不是新 auto pipeline 页面，而是旧的主榜单解析器**。

`err.log` 里的这些：
- `src.leaderboard.read_evals [WARNING] Skipping invalid result file ...`
- `Missing model_name in result file`

说明 `read_evals.py` 正在把 `lb_eval/results/results_*.json` 当成**老 leaderboard 结果格式**来读。但你现在写回的是新的聚合格式，核心字段是：
- `pipeline`
- `model_id`
- `artifact_name`
- `generated_at`
- `run_dir`
- `quant_summary`
- `accuracy`

这里**没有**老格式要求的 `model_name`，所以旧解析器就把它们全 skip 了。

另外还有第二层原因：这个 Intel 版代码当前配置的是去拉 **`lb_eval` 仓库** 的 `requests/results`，而 `LLM Benchmark` 主页面的 `read_evals.py` 仍然是按**旧 schema + 旧 request 匹配逻辑**工作的，所以日志里还会看到大量：

- `Could not find request file for ...`

这会导致 legacy 主榜单最后是 `0` 行。

我已经做了一个修正：
- **`src/leaderboard/read_evals.py` 现在会识别 auto pipeline 聚合结果，并静默跳过，不再把它们报成 invalid warning。**

- **`Auto Pipeline Results` 页面能读到 9 条记录。**

1. **Auto Pipeline Results 页面是正常的**，它会显示你新的 `results_*.json`。
2. **LLM Benchmark 主页面不会显示这批数据**，因为它还是 legacy 解析逻辑，不兼容 `lb_eval` 的新聚合格式。

2. name: auto_eval_vllm
3. description: Automatically evaluate quantized LLM models using vLLM inference engine and lm-evaluation-harness. Supports CUDA GPU with multi-GPU tensor parallelism. Detects Auto-Round quantization format and configures appropriate settings.

14. 
15. # Auto-Eval (vLLM) Skill
16. 
17. Use this skill when users want to evaluate quantized LLM models (especially Auto-Round quantized models) using vLLM and lm-evaluation-harness on NVIDIA CUDA GPUs.
18. 
19. ## Overview
20. 
21. This skill provides a complete workflow for:
22. - **Detecting quantization format** from model metadata
23. - **Configuring vLLM** for CUDA with multi-GPU tensor parallelism
24. - **Running lm-eval** benchmarks (e.g., piqa, hellaswag, mmlu)
25. - **Handling OOM errors** with multi-GPU and memory tuning
26. 
27. **Supported tasks**: piqa, hellaswag, mmlu, arc, gsm8k, and many more via lm-eval
28. 
29. ---
30. 
31. ## Input Parameters
32. 
33. | Parameter | Description | Required | Default |
34. |-----------|-------------|----------|---------|
35. | `model_path` | Path to quantized model (local or HF) | Yes | - |
36. | `task` | Evaluation task (e.g., piqa, mmlu) | Yes | - |
37. | `output_path` | Directory for results | No | `./lm_eval_results` |
38. | `batch_size` | Batch size for evaluation | No | `1` |
39. | `num_gpus` | Number of GPUs for tensor parallelism | No | `1` |
40. | `device` | Device (cuda, cpu) | No | `cuda` |
41. | `max_model_len` | Max sequence length | No | `8192` |
42. | `gpu_memory_utilization` | VRAM fraction | No | `0.9` |
43. 
44. ## Environment / Dependency Rules (CRITICAL)
45. 
46. Prefer reusing an existing system venv before creating a new one:
47. 
48. ```bash
49. if [ -x /root/.venv/bin/python ]; then
50.   VENV_PY=/root/.venv/bin/python
51. else
52.   python3 -m venv --system-site-packages {output_path}/venv
53.   VENV_PY={output_path}/venv/bin/python
54. fi
55. ```
56. 
57. Rules:
58. 
59. 1. Use `uv pip`, not plain `pip install`, for dependency installation
60. 2. If `torch` already imports from the reused environment, keep it
61. 3. If `flash_attn` already imports from the reused environment, keep it
62. 4. Only reinstall `torch` / `flash_attn` when they are missing or clearly incompatible
63. 
64. ---
65. 
66. ## Step 1: Analyze Model and Detect Quantization Format
67. 
68. ### Check quantization_config.json
69. 
70. ```bash
71. cat {model_path}/quantization_config.json
72. ```
73. 
74. **Common quantization formats and vLLM support:**
75. 
76. | Format | packing_format | vLLM Support | Device |
77. |--------|---------------|-------------|--------|
78. | auto_gptq | `auto_gptq` | ✓ (symmetric) | CUDA |
79. | auto_awq | `auto_awq` | ✓ (asymmetric) | CUDA |
80. | auto_round | `auto_round:auto_gptq` | ✓ | CUDA |
81. | llm_compressor | `auto_round:llm_compressor` | ✓ (MXFP4/NVFP4) | CUDA |
82. | GGUF | `gguf` | ✓ (llama.cpp) | CPU |
83. 
84. ### Example quantization_config.json for different formats:
85. 
86. **Auto-GPTQ format:**
87. ```json
88. {
89.   "bits": 4,
90.   "group_size": 128,
91.   "sym": true,
92.   "quant_method": "auto-gptq",
93.   "packing_format": "auto_gptq"
94. }
95. ```
96. 
97. **Auto-Round format:**
98. ```json
99. {
100.   "bits": 4,
101.   "group_size": 128,
102.   "sym": true,
103.   "quant_method": "auto-round",
104.   "packing_format": "auto_round:auto_gptq"
105. }
106. ```
107. 
108. **LLM-Compressor (MXFP4) format:**
109. ```json
110. {
111.   "quant_method": "compressed-tensors",
112.   "format": "float-quantized",
113.   "config_groups": {...},
114.   "provider": "auto-round"
115. }
116. ```
117. 
118. ---
119. 
120. ## Step 2: Configure vLLM Model Args
121. 
122. Based on quantization format and GPU count, configure appropriate vLLM arguments:
123. 
124. ### For Single GPU (num_gpus=1)
125. 
126. **Recommended settings:**
127. ```bash
128. --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,\
129. dtype=bfloat16,\
130. tensor_parallel_size=1,\
131. max_model_len=8192,\
132. gpu_memory_utilization=0.9
133. ```
134. 
135. ### For Multi-GPU (num_gpus > 1)
136. 
137. **Recommended settings using tensor parallelism:**
138. ```bash
139. --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,\
140. dtype=bfloat16,\
141. tensor_parallel_size=$NUM_GPUS,\
142. max_model_len=8192,\
143. gpu_memory_utilization=0.9
144. ```
145. 
146. ### Key Parameters Explained
147. 
148. | Parameter | Description | Recommended |
149. |-----------|-------------|-------------|
150. | `dtype` | Data type | `bfloat16` for CUDA |
151. | `tensor_parallel_size` | Number of GPUs for tensor parallelism | 1 (single), N (multi-GPU) |
152. | `max_model_len` | Max sequence length | 8192 (adjust based on VRAM) |
153. | `gpu_memory_utilization` | VRAM fraction | 0.9 (leaves ~10% headroom) |
154. | `max_gen_toks` | Max tokens to generate | 2048 |
155. | `enforce_eager` | Disable CUDA graph | **Not needed on CUDA** (unlike XPU) |
156. 
157. ### Format-Specific Model Args
158. 
159. **For auto_gptq / auto_round format:**
160. ```
161. pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,tensor_parallel_size=1,max_model_len=8192,gpu_memory_utilization=0.9
162. ```
163. 
164. **For llm_compressor (MXFP4/NVFP4) format:**
165. ```
166. pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,tensor_parallel_size=1,max_model_len=8192,gpu_memory_utilization=0.9
167. ```
168. 
169. ---
170. 
171. ## Step 3: Run lm-eval
172. 
173. ### Basic Command (Single GPU)
174. 
175. ```bash
176. lm_eval \
177.     --model vllm \
178.     --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,tensor_parallel_size=1,max_model_len=8192,gpu_memory_utilization=0.9 \
179.     --tasks piqa \
180.     --batch_size 1 \
181.     --output_path lm_eval_results \
182.     --device cuda
183. ```
184. 
185. ### Multi-GPU Command (User specifies GPU count)
186. 
187. ```bash
188. # Example: use 2 GPUs (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1)
189. export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1
190. export NUM_GPUS=2
191. 
192. lm_eval \
193.     --model vllm \
194.     --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,tensor_parallel_size=$NUM_GPUS,max_model_len=8192,gpu_memory_utilization=0.9 \
195.     --tasks piqa \
196.     --batch_size 1 \
197.     --output_path lm_eval_results \
198.     --device cuda
199. ```
200. 
201. ### Running Multiple Tasks
202. 
203. ```bash
204. # Multiple tasks
205. lm_eval \
206.     --model vllm \
207.     --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,tensor_parallel_size=1,gpu_memory_utilization=0.9 \
208.     --tasks piqa,hellaswag,mmlu \
209.     --batch_size 1 \
210.     --output_path lm_eval_results \
211.     --device cuda
212. 
213. # Task group
214. lm_eval \
215.     --model vllm \
216.     --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,tensor_parallel_size=1,gpu_memory_utilization=0.9 \
217.     --tasks arc_easy,arc_challenge,piqa,hellaswag \
218.     --batch_size 1 \
219.     --device cuda
220. ```
221. 
222. ### Using lm_eval Python API
223. 
224. ```python
225. import lm_eval
226. 
227. results = lm_eval.simple_evaluate(
228.     model="vllm",
229.     model_args="pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,tensor_parallel_size=1,max_model_len=8192,gpu_memory_utilization=0.9",
230.     tasks="piqa",
231.     batch_size="auto",
232.     device="cuda"
233. )
234. 
235. print(results["results"])
236. print(results["versions"])
237. ```

30. 
31. def utc_now() -> str:
32.     return time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())
33. 
34. 
35. def file_timestamp() -> str:
36.     return time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d-%H-%M-%S", time.localtime())

38. 
39. def sanitize_name(value: str) -> str:
40.     return value.replace("/", "_").replace(" ", "_")

43. def looks_like_quantized_artifact(model_short: str) -> bool:
44.     lowered = model_short.lower()
45.     markers = (
46.         "-autoround-",
47.         "-gptq",
48.         "-awq",
49.         ".gguf",
50.         "-gguf",
51.         "llm-compressor",
52.     )
53.     return any(marker in lowered for marker in markers)

56. def run_git(args: list[str], cwd: Path, check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
57.     return subprocess.run(
58.         ["git", *args],
59.         cwd=str(cwd),
60.         text=True,
61.         capture_output=True,
62.         check=check,
63.     )
64. 
65. 
66. def clone_repo(repo_url: str, target_dir: Path) -> None:
67.     target_dir.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
68.     result = subprocess.run(
69.         ["git", "clone", repo_url, str(target_dir)],
70.         text=True,
71.         capture_output=True,
72.         check=False,
73.     )
74.     if result.returncode != 0:
75.         raise RuntimeError(result.stderr.strip() or result.stdout.strip() or "git clone failed")

78. def ensure_git_config(repo_dir: Path, user_name: str, user_email: str) -> None:
79.     run_git(["config", "user.name", user_name], repo_dir)
80.     run_git(["config", "user.email", user_email], repo_dir)

83. def build_auth_url(repo_url: str, token: str | None) -> str:
84.     if not token:
85.         return repo_url
86.     parts = urlsplit(repo_url)
87.     if parts.scheme != "https":
88.         return repo_url
89.     netloc = f"x-access-token:***REDACTED***@{parts.netloc}"
90.     return urlunsplit((parts.scheme, netloc, parts.path, parts.query, parts.fragment))
91. 
92. 
93. def load_json(path: Path) -> dict | None:
94.     if not path.exists():
95.         return None
96.     with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
97.         return json.load(handle)
98. 
99. 
100. def copy_file(src: Path, dst: Path, copied: list[str]) -> None:
101.     if not src.exists() or not src.is_file():
102.         return
103.     dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
104.     shutil.copy2(src, dst)
105.     copied.append(str(dst))
106. 
107. 
108. def copy_tree(src: Path, dst: Path, copied: list[str]) -> None:
109.     if not src.exists() or not src.is_dir():
110.         return
111.     if dst.exists():
112.         shutil.rmtree(dst)
113.     shutil.copytree(src, dst)
114.     copied.append(str(dst))
115.

117. def detect_artifact_name(model_id: str, scheme: str, quant_summary: dict | None) -> str:
118.     if quant_summary:
119.         hf_repo = quant_summary.get("hf_repo")
120.         if isinstance(hf_repo, str) and hf_repo.strip():
121.             return hf_repo.rstrip("/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
122. 
123.     model_short = model_id.split("/", 1)[-1] if "/" in model_id else model_id
124.     if looks_like_quantized_artifact(model_short):
125.         return sanitize_name(model_short)
126.     return sanitize_name(f"{model_short}-autoround-{scheme}")

129. def resolve_repo_dir(repo_dir_arg: str, clone_dir_arg: str, repo_url: str, token: str | None) -> Path:
130.     repo_dir_raw = (repo_dir_arg or "").strip()
131.     clone_dir_raw = (clone_dir_arg or "").strip()
132.     default_clone_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "lb_eval"
133. 
134.     if repo_dir_raw:
135.         repo_dir = Path(repo_dir_raw).resolve()
136.     else:
137.         repo_dir = Path(clone_dir_raw).resolve() if clone_dir_raw else default_clone_dir.resolve()
138. 
139.     if (repo_dir / ".git").exists():
140.         return repo_dir
141. 
142.     if repo_dir.exists():
143.         if any(repo_dir.iterdir()):
144.             raise RuntimeError(f"target repo dir exists but is not a git repo: {repo_dir}")
145.     else:
146.         repo_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
147. 
148.     if not repo_url:
149.         raise RuntimeError("GIT_REPO is required when the local git repo is missing")
150. 
151.     auth_url = build_auth_url(repo_url, token)
152.     print(f"[github-upload] Cloning repo into: {repo_dir}")
153.     shutil.rmtree(repo_dir)
154.     clone_repo(auth_url, repo_dir)
155.     if auth_url != repo_url:
156.         run_git(["remote", "set-url", "origin", repo_url], repo_dir)
157.     return repo_dir

14. 
15. # Auto-Eval Skill
16. 
17. Use this skill when users want to evaluate quantized LLM models (especially Auto-Round quantized models) using HuggingFace backend and lm-evaluation-harness on CUDA GPUs.
18. 
19. ## Overview
20. 
21. This skill provides a complete workflow for:
22. - **Detecting quantization format** from model metadata
23. - **Configuring HF backend** for CUDA with multi-GPU support
24. - **Running lm-eval** benchmarks (e.g., piqa, hellaswag, mmlu)
25. - **Handling OOM errors** with multi-GPU suggestions
26. 
27. **Supported tasks**: piqa, hellaswag, mmlu, arc, gsm8k, and many more via lm-eval
28. 
29. ---
30. 
31. ## Input Parameters
32. 
33. | Parameter | Description | Required | Default |
34. |-----------|-------------|----------|---------|
35. | `model_path` | Path to quantized model (local or HF) | Yes | - |
36. | `task` | Evaluation task (e.g., piqa, mmlu) | Yes | - |
37. | `output_path` | Directory for results | No | `./lm_eval_results` |
38. | `batch_size` | Batch size for evaluation | No | `1` |
39. | `num_gpus` | Number of GPUs to use for inference | No | `1` |
40. | `max_model_len` | Max sequence length | No | `8192` |
41. | `trust_remote_code` | Allow custom model code | No | `True` |
42. 
43. ## Environment / Dependency Rules (CRITICAL)
44. 
45. Prefer reusing an existing system venv before creating a new one:
46. 
47. ```bash
48. if [ -x /root/.venv/bin/python ]; then
49.   VENV_PY=/root/.venv/bin/python
50. else
51.   python3 -m venv --system-site-packages {output_path}/venv
52.   VENV_PY={output_path}/venv/bin/python
53. fi
54. ```
55. 
56. Rules:
57. 
58. 1. Use `uv pip`, not plain `pip install`, for dependency installation
59. 2. If `torch` already imports from the reused environment, keep it
60. 3. If `flash_attn` already imports from the reused environment, keep it
61. 4. Only reinstall `torch` / `flash_attn` when they are missing or clearly incompatible
62. 
63. ---
64. 
65. ## Step 1: Analyze Model and Detect Quantization Format
66. 
67. ### Check quantization_config.json
68. 
69. ```bash
70. # For Auto-Round quantized models
71. cat {model_path}/quantization_config.json
72. ```
73. 
74. **Common quantization formats and HF support:**
75. 
76. | Format | packing_format | HF Support | Device |
77. |--------|---------------|-------------|--------|
78. | auto_gptq | `auto_gptq` | ✓ | CUDA |
79. | auto_awq | `auto_awq` | ✓ | CUDA |
80. | auto_round | `auto_round:auto_gptq` | ✓ | CUDA |
81. | llm_compressor | `auto_round:llm_compressor` | ✓ | CUDA |
82. | GGUF | `gguf` | ✓ (llama.cpp) | CPU |
83. 
84. ### Example quantization_config.json for different formats:
85. 
86. **Auto-Round format:**
87. ```json
88. {
89.   "bits": 4,
90.   "group_size": 128,
91.   "sym": true,
92.   "quant_method": "auto-round",
93.   "packing_format": "auto_round:auto_gptq"
94. }
95. ```
96. 
97. **LLM-Compressor (MXFP4) format:**
98. ```json
99. {
100.   "quant_method": "compressed-tensors",
101.   "format": "float-quantized",
102.   "config_groups": {...},
103.   "provider": "auto-round"
104. }
105. ```
106. 
107. ---
108. 
109. ## Step 2: Configure HF Model Args
110. 
111. Based on quantization format and GPU count, configure appropriate HF arguments:
112. 
113. ### For Single GPU (num_gpus=1)
114. 
115. **Recommended settings:**
116. ```bash
117. --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,\
118. dtype=bfloat16,\
119. device_map=auto,\
120. trust_remote_code=True
121. ```
122. 
123. ### For Multi-GPU (num_gpus > 1)
124. 
125. **Recommended settings using device_map + parallelized:**
126. ```bash
127. --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,\
128. dtype=bfloat16,\
129. device_map=auto,\
130. parallelize=True,\
131. trust_remote_code=True
132. ```
133. 
134. **Alternative: tensor_parallel via model_args (for vLLM backend):**
135. ```bash
136. --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,\
137. dtype=bfloat16,\
138. tensor_parallel_size=$NUM_GPUS,\
139. trust_remote_code=True
140. ```
141. 
142. ### Key Parameters Explained
143. 
144. | Parameter | Description | Recommended |
145. |-----------|-------------|-------------|
146. | `dtype` | Data type | `bfloat16` for CUDA |
147. | `device_map` | Device placement | `auto` for automatic |
148. | `parallelize` | Multi-GPU parallelization | `True` when num_gpus > 1 |
149. | `trust_remote_code` | Allow custom model code | `True` |
150. | `max_model_len` | Max sequence length | 8192 (adjust based on VRAM) |
151. 
152. ### Format-Specific Model Args
153. 
154. **For auto_gptq format:**
155. ```bash
156. --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,trust_remote_code=True
157. ```
158. 
159. **For auto_round format:**
160. ```bash
161. --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,trust_remote_code=True
162. ```
163. 
164. **For llm_compressor (MXFP4/NVFP4) format:**
165. ```bash
166. --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,trust_remote_code=True
167. ```
168. 
169. ---
170. 
171. ## Step 3: Run lm-eval
172. 
173. ### Basic Command (Single GPU)
174. 
175. ```bash
176. lm_eval \
177.     --model hf \
178.     --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,trust_remote_code=True \
179.     --tasks piqa \
180.     --batch_size 1 \
181.     --output_path lm_eval_results \
182.     --device cuda
183. ```
184. 
185. ### Multi-GPU Command (User specifies GPU count)
186. 
187. ```bash
188. # Example: use 2 GPUs (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1)
189. export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1
190. export NUM_GPUS=2
191. 
192. lm_eval \
193.     --model hf \
194.     --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,parallelize=True,trust_remote_code=True \
195.     --tasks piqa \
196.     --batch_size 1 \
197.     --output_path lm_eval_results \
198.     --device cuda
199. ```
200. 
201. ### Running Multiple Tasks
202. 
203. ```bash
204. # Multiple tasks
205. lm_eval \
206.     --model hf \
207.     --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,trust_remote_code=True \
208.     --tasks piqa,hellaswag,mmlu \
209.     --batch_size 1 \
210.     --output_path lm_eval_results \
211.     --device cuda
212. 
213. # Task group
214. lm_eval \
215.     --model hf \
216.     --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,trust_remote_code=True \
217.     --tasks arc_easy,arc_challenge,piqa,hellaswag \
218.     --batch_size 1 \
219.     --device cuda
220. ```
221. 
222. ### Using lm_eval Python API
223. 
224. ```python

226. 
227. results = lm_eval.simple_evaluate(
228.     model="hf",
229.     model_args="pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,trust_remote_code=True",
230.     tasks="piqa",

232.     device="cuda"
233. )
234.

237. ```

83. def build_auth_url(repo_url: str, token: str | None) -> str:

88.         return repo_url
89.     netloc = f"x-access-token:***REDACTED***@{parts.netloc}"
90.     return urlunsplit((parts.scheme, netloc, parts.path, parts.query, parts.fragment))

129. def resolve_repo_dir(repo_dir_arg: str, clone_dir_arg: str, repo_url: str, token: str | None) -> Path:
130.     repo_dir_raw = (repo_dir_arg or "").strip()
131.     clone_dir_raw = (clone_dir_arg or "").strip()
132.     default_clone_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "lb_eval"
133. 
134.     if repo_dir_raw:
135.         repo_dir = Path(repo_dir_raw).resolve()
136.     else:
137.         repo_dir = Path(clone_dir_raw).resolve() if clone_dir_raw else default_clone_dir.resolve()
138. 
139.     if (repo_dir / ".git").exists():
140.         return repo_dir
141. 
142.     if repo_dir.exists():
143.         if any(repo_dir.iterdir()):
144.             raise RuntimeError(f"target repo dir exists but is not a git repo: {repo_dir}")
145.     else:
146.         repo_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
147. 
148.     if not repo_url:
149.         raise RuntimeError("GIT_REPO is required when the local git repo is missing")
150. 
151.     auth_url = build_auth_url(repo_url, token)
152.     print(f"[github-upload] Cloning repo into: {repo_dir}")
153.     shutil.rmtree(repo_dir)
154.     clone_repo(auth_url, repo_dir)
155.     if auth_url != repo_url:
156.         run_git(["remote", "set-url", "origin", repo_url], repo_dir)
157.     return repo_dir

14. 
15. # Auto-Eval Skill
16. 
17. Use this skill when users want to evaluate quantized LLM models (especially Auto-Round quantized models) using HuggingFace backend and lm-evaluation-harness on CUDA GPUs.
18. 
19. ## Overview
20. 
21. This skill provides a complete workflow for:
22. - **Detecting quantization format** from model metadata
23. - **Configuring HF backend** for CUDA with multi-GPU support
24. - **Running lm-eval** benchmarks (e.g., piqa, hellaswag, mmlu)
25. - **Handling OOM errors** with multi-GPU suggestions
26. 
27. **Supported tasks**: piqa, hellaswag, mmlu, arc, gsm8k, and many more via lm-eval
28. 
29. ---
30. 
31. ## Input Parameters
32. 
33. | Parameter | Description | Required | Default |
34. |-----------|-------------|----------|---------|
35. | `model_path` | Path to quantized model (local or HF) | Yes | - |
36. | `task` | Evaluation task (e.g., piqa, mmlu) | Yes | - |
37. | `output_path` | Directory for results | No | `./lm_eval_results` |
38. | `batch_size` | Batch size for evaluation | No | `1` |
39. | `num_gpus` | Number of GPUs to use for inference | No | `1` |
40. | `max_model_len` | Max sequence length | No | `8192` |
41. | `trust_remote_code` | Allow custom model code | No | `True` |
42. 
43. ---
44. 
45. ## Step 1: Analyze Model and Detect Quantization Format
46. 
47. ### Check quantization_config.json
48. 
49. ```bash
50. # For Auto-Round quantized models
51. cat {model_path}/quantization_config.json
52. ```
53. 
54. **Common quantization formats and HF support:**
55. 
56. | Format | packing_format | HF Support | Device |
57. |--------|---------------|-------------|--------|
58. | auto_gptq | `auto_gptq` | ✓ | CUDA |
59. | auto_awq | `auto_awq` | ✓ | CUDA |
60. | auto_round | `auto_round:auto_gptq` | ✓ | CUDA |
61. | llm_compressor | `auto_round:llm_compressor` | ✓ | CUDA |
62. | GGUF | `gguf` | ✓ (llama.cpp) | CPU |
63. 
64. ### Example quantization_config.json for different formats:
65. 
66. **Auto-Round format:**
67. ```json
68. {
69.   "bits": 4,
70.   "group_size": 128,
71.   "sym": true,
72.   "quant_method": "auto-round",
73.   "packing_format": "auto_round:auto_gptq"
74. }
75. ```
76. 
77. **LLM-Compressor (MXFP4) format:**
78. ```json
79. {
80.   "quant_method": "compressed-tensors",
81.   "format": "float-quantized",
82.   "config_groups": {...},
83.   "provider": "auto-round"
84. }
85. ```
86. 
87. ---
88. 
89. ## Step 2: Configure HF Model Args
90. 
91. Based on quantization format and GPU count, configure appropriate HF arguments:
92. 
93. ### For Single GPU (num_gpus=1)
94. 
95. **Recommended settings:**
96. ```bash
97. --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,\
98. dtype=bfloat16,\
99. device_map=auto,\
100. trust_remote_code=True
101. ```
102. 
103. ### For Multi-GPU (num_gpus > 1)
104. 
105. **Recommended settings using device_map + parallelized:**
106. ```bash
107. --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,\
108. dtype=bfloat16,\
109. device_map=auto,\
110. parallelize=True,\
111. trust_remote_code=True
112. ```
113. 
114. **Alternative: tensor_parallel via model_args (for vLLM backend):**
115. ```bash
116. --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,\
117. dtype=bfloat16,\
118. tensor_parallel_size=$NUM_GPUS,\
119. trust_remote_code=True
120. ```
121. 
122. ### Key Parameters Explained
123. 
124. | Parameter | Description | Recommended |
125. |-----------|-------------|-------------|
126. | `dtype` | Data type | `bfloat16` for CUDA |
127. | `device_map` | Device placement | `auto` for automatic |
128. | `parallelize` | Multi-GPU parallelization | `True` when num_gpus > 1 |
129. | `trust_remote_code` | Allow custom model code | `True` |
130. | `max_model_len` | Max sequence length | 8192 (adjust based on VRAM) |
131. 
132. ### Format-Specific Model Args
133. 
134. **For auto_gptq format:**
135. ```bash
136. --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,trust_remote_code=True
137. ```
138. 
139. **For auto_round format:**
140. ```bash
141. --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,trust_remote_code=True
142. ```
143. 
144. **For llm_compressor (MXFP4/NVFP4) format:**
145. ```bash
146. --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,trust_remote_code=True
147. ```
148. 
149. ---
150. 
151. ## Step 3: Run lm-eval
152. 
153. ### Basic Command (Single GPU)
154. 
155. ```bash
156. lm_eval \
157.     --model hf \
158.     --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,trust_remote_code=True \
159.     --tasks piqa \
160.     --batch_size 1 \
161.     --output_path lm_eval_results \
162.     --device cuda
163. ```
164. 
165. ### Multi-GPU Command (User specifies GPU count)
166. 
167. ```bash
168. # Example: use 2 GPUs (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1)
169. export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1
170. export NUM_GPUS=2
171. 
172. lm_eval \
173.     --model hf \
174.     --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,parallelize=True,trust_remote_code=True \
175.     --tasks piqa \
176.     --batch_size 1 \
177.     --output_path lm_eval_results \
178.     --device cuda
179. ```
180. 
181. ### Running Multiple Tasks
182. 
183. ```bash
184. # Multiple tasks
185. lm_eval \
186.     --model hf \
187.     --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,trust_remote_code=True \
188.     --tasks piqa,hellaswag,mmlu \
189.     --batch_size 1 \
190.     --output_path lm_eval_results \
191.     --device cuda
192. 
193. # Task group
194. lm_eval \
195.     --model hf \
196.     --model_args pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,trust_remote_code=True \
197.     --tasks arc_easy,arc_challenge,piqa,hellaswag \
198.     --batch_size 1 \
199.     --device cuda
200. ```
201. 
202. ### Using lm_eval Python API
203. 
204. ```python
205. import lm_eval
206. 
207. results = lm_eval.simple_evaluate(
208.     model="hf",
209.     model_args="pretrained=./quantized_model,dtype=bfloat16,device_map=auto,trust_remote_code=True",
210.     tasks="piqa",
211.     batch_size="auto",
212.     device="cuda"
213. )
214. 
215. print(results["results"])
216. print(results["versions"])
217. ```
218.

21. This skill provides a complete workflow for:
